subject: Post-demo: Clearline performance readiness + PoC acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@clearlinehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jul 2028 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Post-demo: Clearline performance readiness + PoC acceptance criteria

Hi Marta / Arjun — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side (short list so we can move into a PoC quickly):

1) Performance targets you confirmed on the call:
   - P99 per-token latency (streaming) target: <= 150 ms
   - Sustained concurrent streaming sessions: ~250 users (burst to 500 for 3–5 minutes)
   - Throughput target: 200k tokens/min aggregate for the PoC window

2) Network path & connectivity asks we need to qualify before PoC:
   - Preferred: VPC peering (direct) from Clearline VPC to Redwood Private endpoint in us-east-1.
   - Fallback: IPSec VPN with static routes — we need pre-shared key and egress IP ranges.
   - TLS termination: Redwood terminates TLS; we need to confirm MTU and any SSL inspection on your edge.

3) Acceptance criteria we propose for the 2-week PoC:
   - Meet P99 latency <= 150 ms for 90% of test traffic over a 48h window.
   - No more than 0.5% packet loss observed on the egress path.
   - Streaming correctness verified with 5 canonical prompt sets (we’ll supply).

4) Action items / owners:
   - Clearline: share network contact + peering request (Marta). Attachments: your SLO spreadsheet + sample traces.
   - Redwood: provide PoC runbook and preflight checklist (Ben to own), share peering IPs and expected egress ranges (Jonas).

I attached a draft PoC runbook and a short template for the acceptance matrix — Ben and Priyom will follow up with a technical checklist. Proposed PoC kickoff: Mon Jul 24 (can shift if your network team needs time).

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0118

Attachments: redwood-poc-runbook-v1.docx (draft), clearline-slo-requirements.xlsx (as discussed)

From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@clearlinehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Arjun Patel <arjun.patel@clearlinehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jul 2028 17:06:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Clearline performance readiness + PoC acceptance criteria

Thanks Jonas — that summary is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 150ms P99 is our internal guideline for interactive tooling; it’s firm for the initial PoC but we may relax for longer generation tasks.
- Concurrency: the 250 number is correct for steady state; the burst to 500 is realistic during business hours.
- Egress: we prefer VPC peering where possible. Our network team will evaluate direct peering and fallback to VPN only if peering is not permitted by our compliance group.

I attached our SLO spreadsheet with some filled-in columns and a short pcap from our staging environment that shows current baseline egress to us-east-1.

I’ve looped in Arjun (network lead) — Arjun, can you review the connectivity asks and tell us whether peering is feasible and how long approvals take?

Marta
Director, Platform Engineering | Clearline Health
marta.ruiz@clearlinehealth.com
Attachments: network-trace-sample.pcap, clearline-slo-requirements.xlsx

From: Arjun Patel <arjun.patel@clearlinehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@clearlinehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Clearline performance readiness + PoC acceptance criteria

Jonas / Marta — quick note from the network side:

- Peering: feasible but we need a CIDR allocation plan and our security team will run a short risk review (~3 business days).
- VPN fallback: we can provision an IPSec tunnel within 24–48 hours once we have the static egress ranges and pre-shared key.
- Requirements we need from Redwood:
  * Expected egress IP ranges (list of /24s or single IPs)
  * ASN info if BGP peering is considered (we prefer static routes for the PoC).
  * A short list of ports/protocols and MTU expectations.

Also: we’ll run an initial throughput stress during a maintenance window to validate no packet fragmentation occurs — please advise recommended probe sizes.

Regards,
Arjun
Network Lead | Clearline Health

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Arjun Patel <arjun.patel@clearlinehealth.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@clearlinehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 12:35:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Clearline performance readiness + PoC acceptance criteria

Arjun / Marta — thanks. Technical checklist for preflight (Ben’s quick list):

- Redwood will supply:
  1) Egress IP set for PoC: 52.48.16.0/24, 54.210.32.0/24 (these will be the NATed egress addresses).
  2) Ports: 443 (TLS) outbound only; we support persistent HTTP/2 streaming connections.
  3) MTU: recommend 1500; if your path applies smaller MTU (e.g., 1400) we can tune framing on the TCP layer.
  4) Probe guidance: we recommend a mix of 1KB, 16KB and 64KB payload samples for throughput and fragmentation checks.

- PoC runbook highlights:
  * Kickoff day: sanity checks (DNS, routing, auth).
  * Day 1–2: steady-state streaming at 250 concurrent sessions for 4h windows.
  * Day 3–4: burst tests up to 500 concurrent for 5m bursts, repeated 10x.
  * Day 5–10: mixed workload with canonical prompt sets to validate correctness under load.

- Monitoring & telemetry: we’ll share a realtime dashboard and ask you to forward packet captures during any anomaly windows.

I’ll attach a trimmed PoC runbook (same doc Jonas shared, v1 with a few technical details filled in).

Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
Attachments: redwood-poc-runbook-v1.docx

Thanks all — this is actionable and we’re aligned. Next steps on our side:

- I’ll open the peering request today and share the ticket TKT-CL-3387 with you. Expect the security review to complete by Wed Jul 26.
- If peering is delayed, we’ll spin up the IPSec VPN on Jul 23 and run initial traffic through the tunnel.
- We accept the PoC kickoff on Mon Jul 24 at 09:00 ET provided Arjun has the tunnel/peering confirmed by then.

Please send the final runbook and the egress IP confirmation (Ben/Jonas). Once we have that, Arjun will schedule the maintenance window for the throughput probe.

Marta
Director, Platform Engineering | Clearline Health
